use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

evidence_cards.content: Common tracking is defined as sharing of a common track number and shifting R² between C² JUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the core objective (goal) of the use case: to enable coordinated tracking across multiple C² JUs by sharing track identifiers and responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: All C² JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the core objective for C² JUs in the context of publishing air and surface surveillance tracks — specifically, to maintain track integrity through automatic decorrelation when initiating real-time tracks. This directly supports the 'goal' slot by stating what the primary actor (C² JU) must achieve: ensuring accurate, non-redundant track publication via decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have initially achieved Active status, or returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the required system state (Active status) and valid transitions (from Inactive/TDS Failure) that must exist before the C2 JU can proceed to transmit tracks, satisfying the precondition requirement.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must be capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a functional capability prerequisite (R² assumption) required for the actor to engage in the track transmission process.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall not transmit air or surface tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific condition (completion of checks) that triggers the transmission of tracks after the system is in Active status.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the specific event (recognition of eligible tracks) and the resulting user/system decision (initiating action) that starts the resolution process described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found, the C² JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a primary action in the main flow when no correlation exists — integrating uncorrelated data into local surveillance state.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated. After decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the core success scenario for automatic decorrelation: detecting decorrelation conditions, breaking association, and initiating a new local track — directly fulfilling the canonical success boundary of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement after decorrelation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies required output fields and values post-decorrelation, constraining how the newly initiated track must be published — part of the successful publication outcome.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the initial step of the main flow for track correlation to prevent dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: All C² JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a mandatory system capability required to perform the main flow steps automatically.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific constraints on the automatic correlation process within the main flow. These rules prevent the system from merging tracks under certain conflicting or redundant conditions, which is a critical part of the 'Publish' logic for surveillance tracks.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction regarding Identity (ID) conflicts and different Mode II codes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific interaction step where the operator can override default automatic restrictions during the correlation/publishing process.

evidence_cards.content: Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

evidence_cards.content: After it has been determined that a common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the decorrelation shall be executed as follows: The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks)... If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message, with an initial ID of Pending.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the core execution steps of the main flow: testing against remote tracks and assigning a new Track Number upon failure to correlate.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a subsequent step in the main flow sequence following the assignment of the new track number.

evidence_cards.content: After initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure, C² JUs capable of assuming R² for air, surface, or land tracks shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the first mandatory step in the main flow: performing validation checks before transmission is allowed.

evidence_cards.content: The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds and for land tracks is 48 seconds. This may be either an automatic or manual function.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the enforced delay (wait time) that occurs as part of the normal interaction sequence before track publication.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the first action step in the main flow after trigger recognition — it initiates the resolution sequence by broadcasting the correlation request.

evidence_cards.content: The message identifies the TN to be retained and the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the content payload of the J7.2 message — critical for defining what data is exchanged during the main flow interaction.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the default successful response behavior (acceptance) and introduces conditional branching points that may lead to alternative or exception flows — but acceptance is the canonical main flow outcome.

evidence_cards.content: If an operator action has been taken which selectively released a new local track for reporting, it shall be transmitted, regardless of the results of correlation testing.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a successful alternative path that diverges from the main flow's requirement to wait for failed automatic correlation tests before transmitting a new local track; it allows immediate transmission based on manual override.

evidence_cards.content: As a system option, common local tracks may be included in the automatic correlation tests performed upon receipt of remote real-time messages or prior to transmission of a local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This represents an optional variant (alternative flow) where the scope of correlation testing is expanded beyond the default set of tracks (active IUs, remote real-time tracks, and other local tracks) to include common local tracks, altering the standard test procedure.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific alternative flow condition where automatic correlation is restricted based on ID conflict, diverging from the main flow of successful correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific alternative flow condition where automatic correlation is restricted based on Mode II code mismatch, diverging from the main flow of successful correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks being updated with local positional data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific alternative flow condition where automatic correlation is restricted for locally derived real-time tracks, diverging from the main flow of successful correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement, even if the other track has Strength greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception to the Strength field restriction, allowing correlation to proceed in a specific case where one track's strength is unspecified.

evidence_cards.content: If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where ID conflict is resolved via voice coordination or restriction confirmation, followed by a single decorrelation test before correlation execution — diverging from the main flow’s automatic decorrelation and correlation failure sequence.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically select as the TN to be dropped a TN which has any of the OCCs listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(6 7). In the absence of such a selection constraint, JUs shall select the higher TN as the TN to be dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative rule for selecting which track number to drop during correlation — overriding the default ‘higher TN’ selection if specific OCCs are present, thus representing a variant path within the correlation process that still leads to successful resolution.

evidence_cards.content: For a track that has both a TN greater than 07777 and a TN less than 07777, as reported in a J7.4 message, the track with TN greater than 07777 shall be used in this comparison.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative handling rule for dual-TN tracks during dropped track selection — using the higher TN (>07777) for comparison even when both high and low TNs exist, which modifies the standard dropped track logic while still achieving successful correlation outcome.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the Target TN of a J10.2 Engagement Status message for a current engagement reported and conducted by own unit, or is the Reference TN or Target TN of a J10.2 message for a current engagement reported by own unit and conducted by another unit, the system shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to transmit the J10.2 message with the Weapon Engagement Status field set to value 8 (Engagement Broken) if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a successful alternative flow where decorrelation occurs in the context of an active engagement, diverging from the standard automatic test failure path by requiring operator alerting and specific message transmission.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message which own unit originated or to which own unit is preparing a reply, the system shall execute the decorrelation and provide operator display of new track status on TNs A and B before release of the J9.0 reply.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative flow triggered by a pending command message, ensuring decorrelation happens before the reply is released, diverging from the standard flow timing.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A is controlled by own unit (subject of J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message), the system shall not automatically decorrelate; if manually decorrelated, it alerts the operator to report termination of control TN A if appropriate, and reports commencement of control of TN B using J10.5 only if initiated by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow where automatic decorrelation is suppressed for controlled tracks, requiring manual intervention and specific reporting actions, diverging from the automatic decorrelation main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If TN A has been paired by own unit (subject of J10.6 message), the system shall decorrelate and alert an operator as a cue to terminate the pairing on TN A and initiate the pairing on TN B if appropriate.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This outlines an alternative flow for paired tracks, requiring operator alerting and pairing management actions upon decorrelation, diverging from the standard unpaired track handling.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a specific alternative flow path where the system diverges from automatic processing to a manual/voice coordination recovery step upon rejection of a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 2.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a constraint on the alternative flow behavior following a rejection event, preventing immediate re-attempt of the failed correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If the automatic correlation test fails (the local track does not correlate with remote tracks), the C2 JU assigns a new track number (TN B) to the local track and initiates a surveillance track report using locally held data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where the main flow's assumption of a 'common local track' (correlation success) is replaced by a decorrelation event (correlation failure), resulting in a new track publication instead of maintaining a shared track.

evidence_cards.content: When the remote report being tested for correlation is a J2.0 Indirect PPLI message with the Originator E/C field set to value 0 (Surface) or 3 (Air), it shall be processed for correlation like a J3.2 air or J3.3 surface (maritime) track with TQ = 7.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative processing path for specific remote message types during correlation testing, diverging from standard local track handling.

evidence_cards.content: JUs may apply one exception to the restriction in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1g(1) and 4.4.4.3.1g(7)(a) above: if either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed, with the Unknown/Hostile track becoming the dropped Track Number (TN-2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a conditional exception allowing automatic correlation despite conflicting IDs under specific engagement status conditions, representing a successful variant flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the above actions result in resolution of the ID conflict, the TN to be retained shall be tested for decorrelation in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.2a before executing the correlation, except the test shall be conducted only once.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a specific alternative path where the standard flow diverges to perform a mandatory single decorrelation test upon resolving an ID conflict via restriction confirmation or voice coordination.

evidence_cards.content: For a track that has both a TN greater than 07777 and a TN less than 07777, as reported in a J7.4 message, the track with TN greater than 07777 shall be used in this comparison.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a variant rule for 'Dropped Track Number Selection' that overrides the general 'select higher TN' constraint when specific track number ranges are involved.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs may also perform manual decorrelation, and may have a capability to require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow where the C2 JU uses manual intervention or confirmation for decorrelation instead of relying solely on the automatic process described in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When the locally held Environment/Category of a track differs from that received in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT = 1) message, the operator shall be alerted — even if the received Environment/Category is not implemented.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative path during track publication where environmental/category mismatch triggers an operator alert instead of automatic acceptance, diverging from the main flow’s assumption of seamless decorrelation and reporting.

evidence_cards.content: If local data and received data differ regarding whether the TN is assigned to a point or to a track, the operator shall be alerted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This represents another alternative flow branch where assignment ambiguity (point vs. track) interrupts automated processing and requires operator intervention before successful publication can proceed.

evidence_cards.content: In case of ID conflicts — where ID difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected — differences must be presented to operators for evaluation; these may also require voice coordination for final resolution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative success path for identity resolution: when automatic correlation fails due to unresolvable ID conflict, human operator evaluation (possibly with voice coordination) becomes the required divergence from the main automated flow to achieve successful track publication.

evidence_cards.content: Receipt of ID data on a TN for which the receiving JU does not have R² and local positional data is not held will automatically be accepted and the remote ID placed in the database for retention.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful outcome where no local context exists — instead of triggering correlation or alerting, the system accepts remote ID outright, bypassing normal decorrelation logic as a valid variant path.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 0 in the J7.2 message, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be acceptable.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow path where the originating JU permits reversal of its own correlation request, diverging from the main flow’s assumption of unidirectional resolution.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 1 in the J7.2 message, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative constraint path where the originating JU explicitly prohibits reversal, forcing receiving IUs to either accept or reject without counter-proposal — altering the negotiation dynamics of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs may originate a reverse correlation request if the RV field allows it (value 0), or must reject the original request if RV=1 and conditions require rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes branching behavior for receiving IUs based on RV field value — this constitutes an alternative successful path (reverse correlation) versus direct acceptance or rejection, diverging from the canonical single-direction resolution in main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Introduces an alternative initiation mode (manual vs automatic) that affects acceptance logic — this represents a variant success path under human intervention, diverging from the default automated resolution assumed in main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 3 (requesting automatic acceptance), it shall automatically accept the correlation unless: (1) tracks are of different E/C or have an existing conflict, (2) one track is simulated and the other live, or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a successful alternative flow where correlation is accepted via specific message parameters, diverging from the main rejection/decorrelation flows.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a post-acceptance state modification that serves as a constraint for the alternative flow involving manual correlation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found, the C² JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system response (integration) when the primary trigger for correlation fails (exception condition).

evidence_cards.content: If J2 messages are not received subsequent to this action and the receiving C² JU still has no local data, the C² JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception flow outcome where the actor relinquishes reporting responsibility due to lack of data following a failed correlation/integration attempt.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative/exception path where data meets specific criteria triggering decorrelation instead of standard correlation.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the recovery behavior (new track number assignment) following the decorrelation exception.

evidence_cards.content: If an operator action has been taken which selectively released a new local track for reporting, it shall be transmitted, regardless of the results of correlation testing.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific exception flow where the standard automatic correlation test logic is bypassed due to manual operator intervention, resulting in immediate transmission despite potential correlation failures.

evidence_cards.content: If the Strength field of either track is set to a value greater than 1, the C2 JU shall not automatically correlate the tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition (Strength > 1) that acts as an exception trigger preventing automatic correlation during the track publication process.

evidence_cards.content: The restriction on automatic correlation based on Strength values does not apply if either track has the Strength field set to 'No Statement'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies an exclusion within the exception flow, specifying when the blocking condition is ignored.

evidence_cards.content: Under the condition of irregular reporting of nonreal-time tracks, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly defines a negative constraint on transmission behavior for a specific exception scenario (irregular reporting), preventing a standard termination message.

evidence_cards.content: System design should allow for an override in cases where operational necessity requires a shorter wait time or none at all.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies an exception handling path that allows bypassing the mandatory minimum wait time (12/48 seconds) defined in the main flow, based on operational necessity.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN will decorrelate (i.e., when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate), the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition under which a correlation request is rejected as an exception flow.

evidence_cards.content: If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN with received RV field set to value 0, and both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a constraint combination that triggers a rejection exception.

evidence_cards.content: If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN with received RV field set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific RV field value that causes immediate rejection of the correlation.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU receives or generates a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection), it shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system response and cooldown timer following a Correlation Rejection exception.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Lists specific conditions that override automatic acceptance, causing the correlation to be rejected.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received, the R² unit is declared inactive.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an exception condition where reporting responsibility (R²) is lost due to receipt of an inactivation message, which interrupts the normal track publication flow and constitutes an error/unexpected path for the C2 JU.

evidence_cards.content: If no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals, another JU may, by operator action only, assume R² for the point, line, or area using the same Reference TN(s).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception scenario where loss of updates triggers a manual handoff of reporting responsibility — representing a failure recovery path that diverges from automatic track maintenance and requires operator intervention.

evidence_cards.content: Failure to properly correlate local track data with respect to remote data can result in a dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific negative outcome (dual designation) resulting from an error in the correlation process, which constitutes the exception condition for this slot.

evidence_cards.content: If the JU assumes R² for a previously-reported track but holds locally derived data other than No Statement (non-NS) for a field which differs from the value accepted for retransmission, the JU shall report the locally derived data instead of the retransmitted value.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception to the standard retransmission flow where local data overrides received data during R² assumption.

evidence_cards.content: As an exception to the override rule, non-NS data for the Platform, Platform Activity, and Specific Type fields received from the controlling unit for the track shall be retransmitted regardless of locally derived data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific constraint on the exception handling path where certain fields must strictly follow the controlling unit's data even if local data differs.

evidence_cards.content: If a track with Valid Data subsequently fails to respond to interrogations, the C2 JU shall not change the status to 'No Data' unless a Clear action is taken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow where expected data loss (failure to respond) does not trigger a state change (to No Data) without explicit operator intervention, preventing unintended data clearing.

evidence_cards.content: Changes from a Valid Data value to a No Data status resulting from the clearing function (J7.5 (ACT = 0)) will not cause the transmission of a change report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception handling rule for the clearing function: although the internal status changes, the system suppresses the normal reporting behavior (transmission of a change report).

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where reporting responsibility is assumed due to timeout of remote updates, which may affect the state or behavior of track publication flows when remote data is stale.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception flow triggered by receipt of a Drop Track message (J7.0 ACT=0), leading to assumption of reporting responsibility under specific conditions — this represents an error/recovery path in track management.

evidence_cards.content: A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0 shall assume R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception condition for assuming reporting responsibility on nonreal-time tracks based on local update events, bypassing normal time-value criteria — relevant to handling edge cases in track publication logic.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message (with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow triggered by reception of degraded-status messages (NPS indicators), allowing assumption of reporting responsibility as a recovery mechanism — directly addresses failure mode handling.

evidence_cards.content: Under the condition where a C2 JU is purging tracks after a specific time interval (considering irregular reporting of nonreal-time tracks), a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception to the standard termination/cancellation protocol (J7.0 transmission) for specific track states (nonreal-time/irregular reporting) that are being automatically purged.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 0 it indicates a reverse correlation would be acceptable, and when the RV field is set to value 1 it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines system response behavior for handling reverse correlation requests during dual designation resolution — constitutes an exception flow path where the receiving IU may reject or accept based on RV value.

evidence_cards.content: Whenever a correlation request is rejected the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies explicit error reporting mechanism (RV=2) when correlation request is rejected — this is a terminal exception outcome in the dual designation resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection (see paragraph 4.7.3.2.c).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes conditional acceptance/rejection logic for manually initiated correlations — represents an exception flow branch where manual initiation overrides automatic rules but still allows for rejection under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, he shall have the following manual actions at his disposal for attempting resolution of the difference: (1) Update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); (3) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); (4) Change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) Decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; (6) Clear operator alert (any mode).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the exception handling path triggered by an IFF/SIF data conflict alert — a specific error condition requiring operator intervention with defined recovery actions, directly fulfilling the 'exception_flow' slot for error/unexpected condition handling.

evidence_cards.content: If the C2 JU receives a J7.2 Correlation message while holding Operational Contingency Constraints (OCCs) on both tracks or conflicting IDs, it shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an explicit exception flow where a specific incoming message type (J7.2) forces the system to override standard correlation logic and reject the action.

evidence_cards.content: In the event of an ID conflict exception where automatic correlation is allowed to break engagement, the Unknown/Hostile track shall be the dropped Track Number (TN-2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory resolution outcome for a specific exception scenario involving conflicting IDs during an engagement status.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates an operator-initiated recovery mechanism (exception flow) when automatic update fails or requires human confirmation — diverging from automatic decorrelation in main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the Retained TN and the Dropped TN decorrelate when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow condition where automatic decorrelation leads to rejection of correlation, preventing successful track merging.

evidence_cards.content: If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN with RV field set to value 0 and the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint, reverse correlation shall be transmitted; if both Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an exception path where presence of OCC on both tracks causes correlation rejection, altering normal correlation behavior.

evidence_cards.content: If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN with RV field set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines another exception condition based on RV field value that forces correlation rejection.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes recovery behavior (operator alert and voice coordination) triggered by correlation rejection — part of exception handling flow.

evidence_cards.content: An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Indicates optional exception handling behavior (alert) for automatic correlation rejections, which may or may not be implemented.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) different E/C or existing E/C conflict, (2) one simulated and one live track, (3) both locally derived real-time tracks — in which case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Lists specific conditions under which even an otherwise acceptable correlation (RV=3) must be rejected — defining terminal exception outcomes.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a post-exception state constraint following manual correlation acceptance, affecting subsequent automated processing — relevant to exception recovery timing.

evidence_cards.content: If a JU without R² receives a J3 message or J7.5 (ACT = 1) message with remote IFF/SIF data differing from locally held data, it shall respond according to Table 4.7-5.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the trigger condition for an exception flow involving data differences between local and remote units.

evidence_cards.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert (as required in Table 4.7-5), they have manual actions available: (1) Update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message; (3) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message; (4) Change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) Decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; (6) Clear operator alert.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the recovery path and resolution steps for the exception of an IFF/SIF data conflict alert.

evidence_cards.content: According to the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix (Table 4.7-5), if a Unit Without R² has 'Current Data' locally and receives 'Valid Data' remotely that constitutes a conflict (C), the action is to not accept data and alert the operator.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides a specific exception outcome (Conflict/Alert) defined in the matrix for handling data discrepancies.

evidence_cards.content: If a JU capable of maintaining IFF/SIF data detects erroneous codes and no other valid codes are available, it must have the capability to delete or clear the erroneous codes so the interface can return to a No Data status.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the exception handling procedure for detecting and clearing erroneous codes to prevent invalid data propagation.

evidence_cards.content: After successful publication of an Inactive or Limited Status Interface Unit (IU) track, the C² JU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity reported as Friend.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state regarding track reporting and identity assignment after the use case completes successfully for IUs.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the final data values and persistence requirements for the track record in the post-success state.

evidence_cards.content: After successful correlation testing, if a new local track tentatively correlates on the initial test but fails correlation on the next test, the new local track shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines one possible postcondition state: transmission of a decorrelated local track after failed second correlation test.

evidence_cards.content: If no tentative correlation is found on the initial test, the new local track shall be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines another postcondition state: immediate transmission of a local track when initial correlation fails — indicating successful publication without further correlation attempts.

evidence_cards.content: A new local track that correlates with another track on each of the first two correlation tests shall be correlated and held as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a third postcondition state: retention as a common local track (not transmitted) upon passing two consecutive correlation tests — representing successful integration into shared tracking context.

evidence_cards.content: Thereafter, the decorrelation rules (see paragraph 4.4.4.3.2) apply to the track.

evidence_cards.content: If an operator action has been taken which selectively released a new local track for reporting, it shall be transmitted, regardless of the results of correlation testing.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an override postcondition: forced transmission of a locally released track irrespective of automated correlation outcomes — reflecting manual intervention success path.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful correlation of a Dropped TN (via receipt of J7.0 ACT=0), if the own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN shall be designated as a common local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the immediate observable system state change to track designation following successful correlation completion.

evidence_cards.content: If the own unit has R² for the Dropped TN and transmits a J7.0 Drop Track message, upon subsequent report of that Dropped TN by another IU, the own unit shall retain the Dropped TN as a remote track and shall not reattempt correlation with the Retained TN for 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the post-success state where the dropped track is retained remotely and a specific non-correlation constraint is applied for a defined duration.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data, when: a. A J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or b. A J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or c. A J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, or d. The Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU assuming R² of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG. The type of surveillance message will depend upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported. The Identity shall be reported as Friend. The Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported. The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the post-assumption behavior after R² is assumed — specifically how the track is reported and what fields are set (e.g., Identity as Friend, PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator as value 1). This supports defining the outcome state after R² shift in the main flow or postconditions, and confirms that R² assumption leads to active reporting with specific field values.

evidence_cards.content: For NonR² JUs, when an ID conflict is indicated, the unit shall inhibit transmission of the J7.0 (ACT = 1) until the surveillance message is received with the Identity Difference Indicator set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides specific evidence for an exception flow path where a JU without R² handles an ID conflict by inhibiting transmission until resolution (indicator set to 0), rather than aborting or immediately handing off to voice coordination.

evidence_cards.content: For NonR² JUs, an alternative option to handling an ID conflict is to take no action with respect to the reported ID; an operator alert may be provided as a system option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a second valid exception flow branch for NonR² JUs where the system does not automatically resolve the conflict but relies on operator awareness via an optional alert.

evidence_cards.content: If a selection conflict occurs due to OCCs on both the Retained TN and the Dropped TN, the correlation shall be abandoned until the next correlation check.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This provides an explicit exception path for dual designation resolution when OCC conflicts exist on both tracks — it terminates the current correlation attempt and defers retry to the next scheduled check, which is a concrete recovery behavior relevant to exception_flow.

evidence_cards.content: The RV field shall be set to: 0 if there is no OCC on the Retained TN; 1 if the Retained TN has an OCC; 3 if the correlation was manually initiated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines conditional system responses (RV field values) based on OCC presence or manual initiation — these are state-setting actions that occur during exception handling (e.g., OCC conflict or manual override), directly constraining how the system behaves in non-standard correlation scenarios.

evidence_cards.content: Transmission of a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall be discontinued upon receipt of a J7.2 message containing one or both of the same TNs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a termination condition for ongoing correlation transmission — this is an exception flow where external input (receipt of conflicting J7.2) causes cessation of local action, preventing redundant or conflicting correlation attempts.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 shall not accept the requested correlation when local or remote data held indicates one or more of the following conditions exist: (1) There is a correlation restriction as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g. In this case the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Explicitly defines a rejection condition for incoming correlation requests based on pre-existing restrictions — this is a terminal exception outcome (correlation rejected) triggered by policy constraints, fitting the exception_flow slot’s requirement for failed/prevented end states.

evidence_cards.content: When an operator receives an IFF/SIF data conflict alert as required in Table 4.7-5, he shall have the following manual actions at his disposal for attempting resolution of the difference: (1) Update local data manually or verify automatic inputs; (2) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 0) Clear IFF/SIF message (any mode); (3) Initiate J7.5 (ACT = 1) IFF/SIF Difference Report message (any mode); (4) Change local data to agree with remote data except in the case of Mode II code; (5) Decorrelate the local data from the remote data, causing the assignment of a new track number to local data; (6) Clear operator alert (any mode).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim details the specific exception handling path for IFF/SIF data conflicts, listing the six manual resolution options available to the operator when a conflict alert is triggered.
